events.headline: Josh Downs reportedly requests a trade as the Colts sell after firing GM Chris Ballard
events.detail: ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Downs, in the final year of his rookie deal, has asked to be traded, and multiple teams have shown interest. Asked Wednesday, Downs said "I'm here today, but whatever comes my way comes my way." He has 26 catches for 307 yards and no TDs in seven games. Indianapolis fired Ballard this week and has already moved linemen Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner; Shane Steichen says Jonathan Taylor has not asked out. The deadline is Nov. 10.
events.so_what: Nothing changes until he is moved. A trade to a team that uses him in the slot full time could raise his target floor, while staying in a selling offense caps it; he is a bench hold, not a start, while it plays out.

source.label: CBS Sports: Josh Downs landing spots after Colts WR reportedly asks out (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder, foot) Questionable for Thursday vs. Carolina after a limited Wednesday walkthrough
events.detail: Golden sat out Monday and Tuesday, then was limited in Wednesday's walkthrough and carries a Questionable tag into Thursday night's home game against Carolina. The foot issue is new this week on top of the shoulder from last week's report; he played 85% of the snaps through both at Detroit in Week 7. Devonte Wyatt is also Questionable. Final word comes with inactives about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Jayden Reed and Skyy Moore remain on IR, so Green Bay's receiver depth is thin.
events.so_what: A Questionable tag on a Thursday game is the worst kind: if he sits you find out about 90 minutes before kickoff with only Sunday players left to swap in. Start him only if your bench has a comparable Sunday or Monday option you can slot in after inactives post; otherwise take the safer play.

source.label: NBC Sports (PFT): Matthew Golden, Devonte Wyatt questionable for Thursday night (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Lamar Jackson (high ankle) back at practice Wednesday in a limited role; Week 8 at Buffalo still unconfirmed
events.detail: Jackson practiced Wednesday for the first time this week; Jesse Minter said he got in "a little bit of limited work." He has not played since injuring the ankle Oct. 4 against Tennessee and sat out the Week 7 loss to Cincinnati with Tyler Huntley starting. Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday he is expected to play Sunday at Buffalo. Not cleared: Thursday and Friday participation and the Friday designation decide it.
events.so_what: Still a forecast. A limited Wednesday is the expected first step; an upgrade to full by Friday puts him straight back in lineups, because his rushing is the premium this format pays for. Keep a Sunday QB fallback until the Friday report.

source.label: NBC Sports: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practicing Wednesday (Oct. 28)

events.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) practices Wednesday in a non-contact jersey; Week 8 vs. Baltimore still a game-time call
events.detail: Moore, out the last two games with a recurring AC joint sprain, practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, working individual drills and catching passes from Josh Allen; Joe Brady had said he would practice. He needs to take contact Thursday or Friday to be on track for Sunday. He followed the same pattern before Week 6, drew a Questionable tag and was ruled out on game day.
events.so_what: Non-contact work is progress, not a clearance. Leave him on the bench unless he is taking contact by Friday, and have a fallback ready if he lands on Questionable again. Baltimore's DEF gets a softer Bills passing game if he sits.

source.label: NBC Sports: DJ Moore (shoulder) will practice on Wednesday (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) sits out Wednesday practice; Jordan Mason in line to lead the Vikings at Detroit
events.detail: Jones did not practice Wednesday. He has played through an MCL sprain since Week 2 and aggravated it on a fourth-quarter run in the Week 7 win over Indianapolis; Monday imaging showed nothing significant and ESPN's Adam Schefter called him day-to-day, with the possibility he plays through it at Detroit. Jordan Mason out-snapped him 38 to 15 in Week 7, his first game off IR, with 15 carries for 68 yards. The Athletic's Alec Lewis has floated the Vikings adding a back before the deadline.
events.so_what: Mason is the Vikings back to start in Week 8 whether or not Jones plays: he already had the lead role before the injury. Jones is a bench hold until he practices; a possible deadline addition is a risk to both.

source.label: NBC Sports: Aaron Jones (knee) will sit out on Wednesday (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs DNP Wednesday, listed with a shoulder injury, after saying he aggravated his ankle vs. Green Bay
events.detail: Gibbs ran 29 times for 116 yards and caught five passes in the 20-17 win over Green Bay, then went down awkwardly on the final play and said afterward he had aggravated his ankle; Dan Campbell said "he should be good." Detroit's first Week 8 report lists him as a non-participant Wednesday with a shoulder injury. Several Lions veterans also sat for rest. Neither his nor Amon-Ra St. Brown's Sunday status has been determined. Detroit hosts Minnesota on Nov. 1.
events.so_what: One missed Wednesday after a 34-touch game is not yet a reason to bench a bell cow, but the injury listing changed and nobody has explained it. Thursday's report is the signal; keep a Sunday fallback ready for his slot until then.

source.label: Detroit Sports Nation: Detroit Lions initial Week 8 injury report (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) sits Wednesday as planned; Lions expect him back at practice Thursday
events.detail: St. Brown tweaked his ankle in the 20-17 win over Green Bay, a game in which he caught nine passes for 153 yards. Detroit's Wednesday report lists him as a non-participant with an ankle injury, which matches what Dan Campbell outlined Monday: sit Wednesday, return Thursday. He carries no Week 8 designation. Detroit hosts Minnesota.
events.so_what: This is the planned version; keep him in lineups and confirm Thursday participation. A second missed day would change the read.

source.label: Detroit Sports Nation: Detroit Lions initial Week 8 injury report (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) aggravated a previous injury; Broncos unsure about Week 8 vs. Kansas City
events.detail: Waddle left late in the Week 7 win at Arizona after a hit on a reverse that Sean Payton later called "awful." Ian Rapoport reports it was an aggravation of the chest injury that limited him in two practices the week before, and his Week 8 status will be decided later in the week. 9News' Mike Klis expects a Questionable tag with hope he plays Sunday against Kansas City. He looks iffy unless he logs a practice by Friday.
events.so_what: Wait on the Friday report before starting him. If he sits, Courtland Sutton is the Broncos receiver to start and Troy Franklin picks up the snaps.

source.label: NBC Sports: Broncos unsure about Waddle for Week 8 (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) opens Week 8 with a limited practice after four straight missed games
events.detail: Aaron Glenn said Hall would be limited in Wednesday's practice, per The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt. Hall first hurt the quad in Week 3 and was inactive in Week 7 against Miami after a DNP Wednesday and two limited sessions. The Jets face Las Vegas on Sunday. Glenn has said Hall is the starter when healthy; Braelon Allen, who is managing an ankle issue of his own, led the backfield in his absence.
events.so_what: Same opening as last week, when he ended up inactive, so a limited Wednesday tells you little. Only a full practice by Friday makes him a start, and even then expect him to share early work with Allen.

source.label: RotoWire: Breece Hall beginning week with limited practice (Oct. 28)

events.headline: Saquon Barkley returns but plays only nine snaps after tweaking his back; Dameon Pierce leaves with an undisclosed injury in a 38-21 loss to Dallas
events.detail: Barkley was active off the Questionable tag and touched the ball on all nine of his snaps: 7 carries for 62 yards and a TD plus 2 catches for 9. He hurt his back on a 29-yard first-quarter run, his last snap came in the third quarter, and he was listed questionable to return with a back injury. Afterward he said the hamstring "came out great" and he does not expect the back to keep him out, deferring to the trainers. Pierce led the backfield with 14 carries for 47 yards and a TD, then left on a fourth-quarter kickoff return; practice-squad call-up Elijah Mitchell finished the game. Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley remain on IR. Philadelphia hosts Washington on Sunday night. As of Tuesday the Eagles had given no update on Pierce, and Mitchell, signed off the practice squad last week, was the only healthy back at the end of the game.
events.so_what: The back is a new injury with no designation yet, so treat Barkley as a Wednesday-practice decision, not a locked start. The per-touch efficiency was there; the snap count was not. If Barkley and Pierce both sit, Elijah Mitchell inherits the work by default, which makes him a speculative add rather than a trusted start until the practice reports say who is healthy.

source.label: ESPN: Barkley hobbled but efficient in loss to Cowboys (Oct. 27)

events.headline: Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) headed to IR, out through at least Week 12; Cam Skattebo expects to be fine after his 124-yard day
events.detail: Giants GM Joe Schoen said Tuesday that Tyrone Tracy Jr. will be placed on injured reserve with the hamstring he hurt in Sunday's overtime win over Houston. It is not season-ending, but IR costs him at least the next four games. Devin Singletary is expected to be the top complement to Skattebo, and the Giants plan to sign Greg Desrosiers off the Chargers' practice squad for depth. Skattebo, back in the lead role after Najee Harris' Oct. 20 release, carried 17 times for 124 yards and a TD, felt something in his own hamstring on a 42-yard overtime run, and told ESPN on Monday he believes he will be fine; there is still no team diagnosis. The Giants are on bye in Week 8.
events.so_what: Skattebo earned the job back on volume and efficiency, so he is a starter-level back once the bye passes, provided his own hamstring checks out. With Tracy on IR, Singletary is the clear second back and the only Giant worth a bench spot as Skattebo insurance. Nobody needs to start a Giant in Week 8.

source.label: RotoWire: Tyrone Tracy bound for IR (Oct. 27)

events.headline: Ladd McConkey back at practice in a non-contact jersey while in concussion protocol; Tre' Harris (hamstring) could return after the bye
events.detail: McConkey practiced Monday in a no-contact jersey as he works through the concussion protocol; it is unclear whether he clears in time for the Chargers' next game. He missed Week 6 with a foot injury before the concussion. Tre' Harris (hamstring) could also return after the bye. Omarion Hampton played 49% of the snaps in a three-back rotation with Kimani Vidal in Week 6.
events.so_what: Practice in a non-contact jersey is a protocol step, not a clearance; he needs to be cleared for contact before he is a start. Hampton's 49% snap share in a rotation keeps him a FLEX at best until the backfield sorts out.

source.label: Fantasy Alarm: NFL injury report, Week 8 (Oct. 27)

events.headline: Rashid Shaheed (knee) avoids the worst case, Mike Macdonald says early word is 'positive'; no timeline for Monday vs. Chicago
events.detail: Shaheed left Seattle's 20-3 win over Kansas City after 22 snaps (two catches on three targets for one yard) following a collision with Jaxon Smith-Njigba. On Monday Mike Macdonald said the early word on the knee is "positive," but gave no timeline. Shaheed had a full left meniscus repair in 2024 that cost him 11 games. LT Charles Cross has a high ankle sprain, with a hoped-for return in one to two weeks. Seattle hosts Chicago next Monday night, which buys an extra day.
events.so_what: Better than feared, but still not a start until he practices. With a Monday kickoff, any lineup holding him needs a fallback that plays earlier in the week.

source.label: RotoWire: Rashid Shaheed avoids worst-case knee issue (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Christian McCaffrey has a mild hamstring strain, Kyle Shanahan "pretty optimistic" for Week 9 after the bye
events.detail: McCaffrey scored on San Francisco's opening drive at Atlanta, sat the second quarter, then returned and finished with 7 carries for 39 yards and a TD plus 6 catches for 61 in the 29-20 loss; Kaelon Black ran for 63 yards and a TD while he was out. On Monday Shanahan called it a mild hamstring strain and said the 49ers are "pretty optimistic" he plays after the Week 8 bye, against Las Vegas.
events.so_what: No lineup decision until Week 9 because of the bye. A mild strain with two weeks to heal is a hold, not a sell. Black is a handcuff, not a start.

source.label: Heavy: Shanahan gives injury timeline update on McCaffrey (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Zach Charbonnet to practice fully with a chance to debut Monday vs. Chicago; Jadarian Price designated to return from IR
events.detail: Charbonnet sat Week 7 after his activation from PUP (torn ACL) and will practice fully this week. Price, a rookie who missed four games on IR with a chest injury, is eligible and will practice. Mike Macdonald would not commit: "Could they both play? Yes. Could neither play? Yes." Emanuel Wilson has been carrying the lead role, and Velus Jones Jr. has a hamstring injury of unknown severity.
events.so_what: Both are forecasts, and the Monday-night kickoff means you will know the inactives only after the rest of your lineup locks. Do not start Charbonnet or Price blind this week. Wilson stays a FLEX until one of them is active, and loses value fast once they are.

source.label: Seahawks.com: This week's plan for Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) set to practice Wednesday after missing two games; Week 8 at Dallas still open
events.detail: Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love is expected to practice Wednesday, per The Arizona Republic's Theo Mackie and the team site's Darren Urban. Love has missed Weeks 6 and 7 with a lingering ankle issue, and Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight split the backfield in his absence. Arizona plays at Dallas on Sunday, and he will likely need several straight practices to get there.
events.so_what: A Wednesday practice is a start, not a clearance; Love likely needs a couple of sessions before he gets a designation, so hold him and check Friday. If he plays, expect a share rather than his early-season workload, which leaves Allgeier and Knight as FLEX-only and the touchdown upside split.

source.label: NBC Sports: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) to practice Wednesday (Oct. 26)

events.headline: Tony Pollard runs 25 times for 129 yards and three TDs with Tyjae Spears inactive in a 27-24 loss to Cleveland
events.detail: With Spears (knee) and Nicholas Singleton inactive, Pollard carried the Tennessee backfield: 25 carries, 129 yards, three rushing TDs, plus three catches for 26 yards, per FantasyPros and PFF. Tennessee rushed for 141 yards as a team. He had scored two touchdowns in his previous 10 games combined. Calvin Ridley (hip) was also inactive, and Elic Ayomanor took his snaps.
events.so_what: While Spears is out Pollard is the whole Titans run game, which makes him an RB2 with touchdown upside. Watch Spears on this week's practice report: his return cuts the volume back to a split.

source.label: FantasyPros: Tony Pollard scores three TDs in Week 7 (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Woody Marks plays 89% of the snaps with David Montgomery (groin) out; Jaylin Noel leaves with a toe injury in a walking boot
events.detail: With Montgomery out a second straight week, Marks took 89% of Houston's snaps and ran 19 times for 66 yards in the overtime loss to the Giants. WR Jaylin Noel left with a turf toe injury, DeMeco Ryans said, and was in a walking boot afterward. Tank Dell played his first game since his 2024 knee injury as Houston used six receivers; Nico Collins ran a route on 80% or more of dropbacks but has drawn five targets in each of his last two games. Houston is on bye in Week 8. By Tuesday Noel's turf toe was still being evaluated, with the severity unclear.
events.so_what: Marks is a volume RB2 for as long as Montgomery sits; Montgomery is a bench hold, not a drop. Noel's injury trims the receiver rotation, which helps Collins' target count more than anyone else.

source.label: PFF: NFL Week 7 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Ollie Gordon II carries 25 times for 103 yards and a TD in Miami's first win; Jaylen Wright (quad) leaves
events.detail: With De'Von Achane out for the season (torn ACL, Week 3), Gordon played 42 of 52 snaps through three quarters and ran 25 times for 103 yards and a TD in the 28-25 win over the Jets. Jaylen Wright hurt his quad late in the third quarter and did not return after eight snaps.
events.so_what: Gordon is now a workhorse on volume alone and a start as an RB2. If Wright misses time, nobody else in this backfield has a role worth rostering.

source.label: PFF: NFL Week 7 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways (Oct. 25)

events.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) ruled out after the first drive in Paris; Alvin Kamara takes every-down work
events.detail: Donaldson, New Orleans' third-down back, hurt his shoulder on the opening drive of the loss to Pittsburgh and was ruled out at halftime. Kamara, limited or out of each of his last nine practices, became the every-down back but produced little. PFF also flags Juwan Johnson's route participation under 60% in each of the last two games. Travis Etienne Jr. is on IR and eligible after the bye.
events.so_what: Kamara gets the whole backfield while Donaldson is out, which makes him a FLEX on volume, though his practice history is a real risk. Etienne's return is what to watch, since it ends the arrangement.

source.label: PFF: NFL Week 7 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) active vs. Carolina, back after three missed games; Emeka Egbuka inactive
events.detail: Mayfield carried a Questionable tag after full practices Wednesday and Thursday. NFL Network reported Sunday he will play wearing a protective glove, and he is not on Tampa Bay's inactive list. Jalon Daniels went 1-2 as the starter with 501 passing yards, three TDs and four INTs. Egbuka (concussion/foot) is inactive.
events.so_what: Mayfield is a usable QB again, but without Egbuka his receiver group is thin, which caps the ceiling this week. Egbuka is a bench hold until he clears protocol. The rest of the Tampa passing game gets a real lift from the QB change.

source.label: CBS Sports: NFL Week 7 inactives and injury tracker (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Josh Jacobs returns as the Packers lead back at Detroit: 54% of the snaps, 11 carries, a receiving TD
events.detail: In his 2026 debut after coming off the commissioner exempt list, Jacobs played just over half of Green Bay's offensive snaps, ran 11 times and caught five passes for 55 yards and a touchdown in the loss to Detroit. Pierre Strong Jr. was pushed down to the RB3 spot. The league's personal-conduct investigation continues and a suspension is still possible.
events.so_what: The snap share should climb as his conditioning returns, and the goal-line and receiving work are already his. Start him as an RB2 from Week 8. The open conduct investigation is the real risk to rest-of-season value.

source.label: PFF: NFL Week 7 recap, immediate fantasy takeaways (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Jonah Coleman leads the Broncos backfield in his first game off IR: 50% of the snaps, 9 carries for 54 yards
events.detail: Coleman, activated from IR the day before, out-snapped RJ Harvey (25%) and J.K. Dobbins (21%) in the 30-16 win over Arizona, adding two catches for 15 yards. Dobbins (6 carries, 1-yard TD) declined interviews afterward; Harvey turned three carries and two targets into 60 yards and a TD. Coleman was the only Denver back without a touchdown. Denver hosts Kansas City in Week 8.
events.so_what: A three-way split with the rookie on top is a start for nobody yet, but Coleman holds the early-down role that matters most here. Treat him as a FLEX-depth add and Dobbins as the one losing value; goal-line work is still unsettled.

source.label: NBC Sports: Coleman operates as Broncos lead back in Week 7 (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. catches 5 of 5 targets for 115 yards and a TD vs. Miami, his second straight big game
events.detail: The rookie first-round pick leads the Jets with a 22% target share and 35% of the air yards across his two healthy games, and New York lined him up in the backfield on a designed red-zone touch. Adonai Mitchell is back from a finger injury, so the three-receiver set is now Cooper, Garrett Wilson and Mitchell. The Jets face Las Vegas in Week 8.
events.so_what: Two games is a small sample and the target pecking order with Mitchell back is unknown, so he is a FLEX option, not a locked starter. The designed red-zone usage is the part that travels: touchdowns score the same in all three leagues.

source.label: NBC Sports: Omar Cooper Jr. stays hot with 5/115/1 vs. Miami (Oct. 25)

events.headline: Contenders weighing offers for Jonathan Taylor; 2-5 Colts will decide over the next three games before the Nov. 10 deadline
events.detail: After Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard, reports named Green Bay, Seattle, Denver and Minnesota among potential suitors. The Colts have not decided whether to move him and plan to watch the next three games. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon reportedly prefers not to trade him. He leads active backs in rushing yards per game (89.9).
events.so_what: Nothing has happened yet, so start him as usual. A trade would move his volume, not erase it; the bigger swing is the backup behind him in Indianapolis, who becomes a stash only if a deal goes through.

source.label: Field Level Media: Contenders considering offer for Colts RB Jonathan Taylor
